title: Together, twenty-seven times
hookLine: prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times better than alone (Bukhari)

cards: Sunset in a small apartment, two roommates home from work, a pot on the stove. The sunset prayer has come in. Each could pray alone, in separate rooms, and be back at dinner in minutes.
Instead one steps forward onto the rug, and the other stands at his right side. One voice says Allahu akbar, and two people bow at once. No mosque, no crowd, no microphone.
A leader, a follower, and a room that smells of onions. Today's word is what those two just made.

teach.b: Jama'ah means congregation, the gathered group. First, the number in today's title.
Ibn Umar reported, in Sahih al-Bukhari, that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said prayer in congregation is better than prayer alone by twenty-seven degrees.

Right beside it, Bukhari records another companion's report that says twenty-five. Scholars offer ways to read the two together; the hadith doesn't explain the arithmetic. Both agree on direction: together is more.
Pickthall's translation of surah two: "bow your heads with those who bow." With. Third, the rows.
The Prophet told them to straighten their rows, and said straightening them is part of establishing the prayer.

Anas, his servant, described them standing shoulder to shoulder and foot to foot. In a row, the person beside you is whoever arrived next, and the row doesn't check anyone's bank balance. Fourth, who is called.
Scholars differ on how binding congregation is for men: the Hanbali school treats it as obligatory, others as a communal duty or a strongly stressed sunnah.
And Bukhari records the Prophet saying: do not keep the women servants of God from the mosques of God.

teach.h: THE WEEK STEPS INTO THE ROW.
teach.b: Now look back at the week. Stand now, at the iqamah. The sunnah around it.
Awake for him. The forenoon prayer. Choose for me.
All but the first can be done alone, in a dark bedroom or a quiet office. The week ends by stepping into the row.

how: Muslims pray in congregation at mosques, in homes and at work, standing in straight rows behind an imam; even two people can pray together, with one leading.

o: the Friday sermon given before the noon prayer
a mosque's council of elders and trustees
praying together in rows, behind one leader

p: shoulder to shoulder, foot to foot

s: every report gives the number twenty-seven
Bukhari records one report with twenty-seven and another with twenty-five.
the Prophet said not to keep women from the mosques
Bukhari: do not keep the women servants of God from the mosques of God.
all schools agree congregation is obligatory for men
the Hanbali school holds it obligatory; others call it a communal duty or a strongly stressed sunnah.

games.q: you arrive late. the rows are formed and there's a small gap beside a stranger. what do the hadith reports point you to?
o: step into the gap and close the row.
games.why: the Prophet told them to straighten their rows, and Anas describes them standing shoulder to shoulder and foot to foot.

practice: See a row in your mind and who might stand in it with you, a neighbor, a parent, a stranger from the bus, and feel where your shoulder would touch theirs.

If you pray, you can pray one prayer today in congregation, at a mosque or with even one other person at home. If you don't, you can share one thing you'd usually do alone: a meal, a walk, a job around the house.

wordCard.voice: Jama'ah. The congregation: prayer in rows, together, counted in the hadith as twenty-seven degrees above prayer alone. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a gathered group, the congregation at prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: together is more. Tomorrow, the voice that speaks to the row on Friday.

sources.q: bow your heads with those who bow
